accepted_interpretation.source_support: If a field K has class number h, its Hilbert class field L has degree governed by h and the same root discriminant as K. If discriminant lower bounds force every nontrivial candidate L of the relevant degree to have root discriminant larger than that preserved value, then L=K and h=1. More generally, analytic bounds first give class-number upper bounds that algebraic methods can lower.
